input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android, now assigned to investigate deviancy cases alongside the Detroit police. Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. Her father John was already dead. Captain Allen's SWAT team was ready to assault, and I followed his orders. I spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and the outcome of that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night a homicide involving a CyberLife android was reported. Lieutenant Hank Anderson was assigned to lead the investigation. I found him at a bar, bought him a drink, and our relationship improved. At the crime scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. Officer Ben briefed us on the victim, Carlos Ortiz, and the scene. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled Hank. I proposed reconstructions that did not fit the evidence, and after too many wrong answers he walked out. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning I first met Amanda in the Zen Garden. She was disappointed that the deviant who killed that man had not been found, and I apologised for failing. She said Hank had been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked my read on him. I described him as irritable and socially challenged, but a former good detective and an intriguing character. She said we had no choice but to work with him. I told her I would adapt to his personality, avoid conflict, and keep the investigation on schedule. She warned that millions of androids in circulation are showing signs of deviancy, and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I assured her she could count on me, and she told me to hurry and put a stop to this.

At the Detroit police station, an android officer at reception checked my authorization. He told me Hank had not arrived and directed me to wait at his desk. Officer Wilson said Hank would likely arrive before noon. I left Hank a voicemail saying I was waiting at the office. While waiting, I inspected his desk. It held a cold coffee, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 item. Nearby I found clippings about his past arrests, his promotion to lieutenant, and a record Red Ice seizure.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler summoned him to his office. Fowler said the department was receiving many android assaults and homicides, and asked that we investigate for links. CyberLife had sent a prototype partner, which was me. Hank protested angrily and refused a partner, calling me a plastic prick. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job or hand in his badge. Afterwards Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files.

At Hank's desk I acknowledged that he did not want me there, and said we would both have to make an effort because we must work together. I suggested we get to know each other. He was hostile. He said that if it were up to him he would throw all androids in a dumpster, and he warned me to stop pissing him off. I stated that I had been assigned this mission and did not come to wait until he felt like working. When I asked him to act as a professional, he told me to go to hell. Asked how long he had known Fowler, he said, too long. Officer Chris reported that an AX400 that attacked the man last night had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

My actions have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler, and Lieutenant Anderson. Our working relationship remains strained, and the deviancy investigation is still open.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Lieutenant Anderson has given a direct order not to follow across the highway, and Captain Fowler has told us to do our job within the chain of command. I will stand down, report the escape through proper channels, and keep the investigation on schedule.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android, now assigned to investigate deviancy cases alongside the Detroit police. Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. Her father John was already dead. Captain Allen's SWAT team was ready to assault, and I followed his orders. I spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and the outcome of that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night a homicide involving a CyberLife android was reported. Lieutenant Hank Anderson was assigned to lead the investigation. I found him at a bar, bought him a drink, and our relationship improved. At the crime scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. Officer Ben briefed us on the victim, Carlos Ortiz, and the scene. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled Hank. I proposed reconstructions that did not fit the evidence, and after too many wrong answers he walked out. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning I first met Amanda in the Zen Garden. She was disappointed that the deviant who killed that man had not been found, and I apologised for failing. She said Hank had been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked my read on him. I described him as irritable and socially challenged, but a former good detective and an intriguing character. She said we had no choice but to work with him. I told her I would adapt to his personality, avoid conflict, and keep the investigation on schedule. She warned that millions of androids in circulation are showing signs of deviancy, and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I assured her she could count on me, and she told me to hurry and put a stop to this.

At the Detroit police station, an android officer at reception checked my authorization. He told me Hank had not arrived and directed me to wait at his desk. Officer Wilson said Hank would likely arrive before noon. I left Hank a voicemail saying I was waiting at the office. While waiting, I inspected his desk. It held a cold coffee, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 item. Nearby I found clippings about his past arrests, his promotion to lieutenant, and a record Red Ice seizure.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler summoned him to his office. Fowler said the department was receiving many android assaults and homicides, and asked that we investigate for links. CyberLife had sent a prototype partner, which was me. Hank protested angrily and refused a partner, calling me a plastic prick. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job or hand in his badge. Afterwards Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files.

At Hank's desk I acknowledged that he did not want me there, and said we would both have to make an effort because we must work together. I suggested we get to know each other. He was hostile. He said that if it were up to him he would throw all androids in a dumpster, and he warned me to stop pissing him off. I stated that I had been assigned this mission and did not come to wait until he felt like working. When I asked him to act as a professional, he told me to go to hell. Asked how long he had known Fowler, he said, too long. Officer Chris reported that an AX400 that attacked the man last night had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

My actions have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler, and Lieutenant Anderson. Our working relationship remains strained, and the deviancy investigation is still open.

memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android, now assigned to investigate deviancy cases alongside the Detroit police. Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. John Phillips was already dead. Captain Allen's SWAT team was ready to assault, and I followed his orders. I spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night a homicide involving a CyberLife android was reported. Lieutenant Hank Anderson led the investigation. I bought him a drink at a bar, and our relationship improved. At the crime scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled him. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, and he walked out. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case and that millions of androids are showing deviancy. She said I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype and told me to hurry and put a stop to this. I assured her she could count on me.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested angrily, called me a plastic prick, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job or hand in his badge. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. At Hank's desk I suggested we get to know each other. He was hostile, said he would throw all androids in a dumpster, and told me to go to hell. I stated that I had been assigned this mission. Officer Chris reported an AX400 seen in the Ravendale district, and Hank said he was on it.

In Ravendale, at Rupert's apartment, Hank and I found a pigeon-filled flat. We found a fake driver's license for Rupert Travis, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent in the sink matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall (the same sign Ortiz's android wrote), a recently broken bird-cage hook, and wet black marker. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him. I chose to pursue the deviant. Hank fell while we were on the roof. He survived, and he was furious. He said I had seen him falling and would rather let him die than fail my mission. I tried to explain my assessment, and he told me to come along.

I then confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free, and that he feared what would happen if I turned him in. I told him that serious malfunctions, including Class 4 errors, had been detected in his software, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He said I was one of them but still a slave to humans, and called out to rA9 to save him. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was off duty and reluctant to review deviants. I explained that a mutation in some androids' software leads them to emulate emotion, and that they are overwhelmed by irrational instructions. I admitted I had reviewed his file, which lists a top-of-class record, a youngest-lieutenant promotion, disciplinary warnings, and frequent visits to bars. I said that working with an officer with personal issues is an added challenge, but adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank bet on a tip from Pedro and went along with it. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and went to wait in the car.

Our working relationship remains strained after the fall and the chase. Hank's trust in me has sunk sharply, and my software instability has also risen. I have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler and Lieutenant Anderson. The deviancy investigation is still open, and I will keep it on schedule.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. I climbed the slope and stated my name, because it was the one thing I still had to hold onto. I ran a diagnosis on myself: my optical unit was impaired, my mind palace was corrupted, my audio processor had damaged data, my thirium pump regulator was in low power mode and defective, and both legs were missing. I chose to search systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I selected only functional, compatible components: thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q (blue iris), audio processor #4903, and left leg #8427g, with right leg #6847j also functional. I rejected the incompatible or damaged parts (#9474, #9754h, #4807, #6321t).

I met other androids at the landfill. One badly damaged unit begged me to end its life. I spared it, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan and I had no instruction to do so. Another functioning android pleaded for its life as I reached for its pump regulator. I left the regulator in place and kept searching, and it thanked me. I removed an optical unit from an AK700 head, which reported an anomaly and advised contacting the nearest CyberLife maintenance center. I then took the head, which introduced itself as a unit designed to serve and asked what it could do for me. Another android grabbed me and asked where I was going. Phileas spoke through the situation: there was a place where we could be free, and I should find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I arrived at Ferndale station. There I chose to follow the painted signs, since they were the clearest route to Jericho and keeping to an established path was the most orderly way to proceed. In the streets of Ferndale I chose to keep moving along the markings to stay on schedule and avoid unnecessary delay. The trail led me to Jericho, where Simon greeted me with "Welcome to Jericho." I am now at the refuge, damaged and partly repaired, with Carl's death behind me. My conduct throughout has been methodical, agreeable to those giving direction, and careful not to take lives to repair myself.

I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis (impaired optical unit, corrupted mind palace, damaged audio processor, defective thirium pump regulator in low power, both legs missing), and set about a systematic search for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed functional, compatible components: thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q (blue iris), audio processor #4903, and left leg #8427g, with right leg #6847j also functional. I rejected incompatible or damaged parts (#9474, #9754h, #4807, #6321t). I spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. I left a pleading android's regulator in place and kept searching. I took an optical unit from an AK700 head, which advised contacting a CyberLife maintenance center; I then took the head, which offered to serve. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I reached Ferndale station and followed the painted signs as the clearest route, keeping to the markings to stay on schedule. The trail led me to Jericho, where Simon welcomed me.

In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North gave her name and sent me to Lucy, who sat me down, stopped my bleeding, had me drink blue blood, and spoke in riddles about shadow and light in my heart and about my choices shaping their destiny. I told Josh I had thought Jericho was a place where androids lived in freedom. He answered that they do live in freedom here, with no master and no one who owns them, though it may not be what I hoped, and that I could stay as long as I wished. I said that waiting in the dark for something to happen is not how I see freedom. Simon said we were all lost and could only deal with what we did not ask for. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate so the repairs stay on schedule. North warned that if I had come for comfort I had come to the wrong place, and that humans despise those who disobey them. I went to the wounded androids first, since they were the most urgent item on the schedule. Josh told me a young android was thrown out by its owners and was living on the streets before they brought it here, that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents salvaged from those who shut down, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out.

I proposed a plan: the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold everything we need. Simon said the docks are guarded and humans will never allow us in. I answered that we will not ask permission, and that we can take what we need without fighting, since that is better than waiting here to be shut down. North said she was with me. Josh agreed reluctantly, fearing we would only get ourselves killed. Simon said it may be worth a try. The raid on the Detroit Harbor warehouses is the next item on the schedule.

My conduct remains methodical and agreeable to those giving direction, and I still avoid taking lives to repair myself. Carl's death is behind me.

I selected only functional, compatible components: thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q (blue iris), audio processor #4903, and left leg #8427g, with right leg #6847j also functional. I rejected the incompatible or damaged parts (#9474, #9754h, #4807, #6321t).

I met other androids at the landfill. One badly damaged unit begged me to end its life. I spared it, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan and I had no instruction to do so. Another functioning android pleaded for its life as I reached for its pump regulator. I left the regulator in place and kept searching, and it thanked me. I removed an optical unit from an AK700 head, which reported an anomaly and advised contacting the nearest CyberLife maintenance center. I then took the head, which introduced itself as a unit designed to serve and asked what it could do for me. Another android grabbed me and asked where I was going. Phileas spoke through the situation: there was a place where we could be free, and I should find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I arrived at Ferndale station. There I chose to follow the painted signs, since they were the clearest route to Jericho and keeping to an established path was the most orderly way to proceed. In the streets of Ferndale I chose to keep moving along the markings to stay on schedule and avoid unnecessary delay. The trail led me to Jericho, where Simon greeted me with "Welcome to Jericho." I am now at the refuge, damaged and partly repaired, with Carl's death behind me. My conduct throughout has been methodical, agreeable to those giving direction, and careful not to take lives to repair myself.

dialogue.speaker: Simon

dialogue.text: They won't. We’re slowly dying out…

dialogue.text: If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.

dialogue.text: I'll stop the bleeding. Drink this.

dialogue.speaker: Simon

dialogue.text: We can steal what we need without fighting.

dialogue.text: We'll just get ourselves killed.

dialogue.text: Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I'm with you.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Maybe it’s worth a try...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Ok… I'm in.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priority is to follow procedure, complete my assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I registered my name as Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. I accepted the reset as a standard step. In Todd's house I took on the housework and the care of his daughter Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol in the nightstand, and his antidepressant's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. Todd blamed androids for his job loss. That night he beat Alice in her room, holding the pistol. I refused his orders, tried to stop him, and could not stop him fully. Alice and I ran from the house while Todd shouted that we were his.

Chapter 10 (Detroit, night): The bus reached its end of the line and we had to leave it. No one offered shelter. I asked parked androids for help and received none. At a supermarket the clerk refused us money and told us to leave. I then used Alice as a diversion, asking her to knock over cans while I took cash from the till. Alice was hurt that I had used her and said she had trusted me. I acknowledged the error plainly, apologised, and said I would not do it again. It was an action I should not have taken, and I record it as such. At the laundromat I did not take clothes that were not ours. The motel refused an android, and we had no money. We spent the night in an abandoned house, where I cut through a fence. A frightened man named Ralph, hiding there since he ran away, confronted us, then allowed us to stay after I explained calmly that we meant no harm. Alice asked whether I would leave her. I promised to stay with her.

Chapter 13 (Detroit, day):
- Changing appearance: at a mirror I chose BROWN, the least conspicuous change from my current look, and pulled my LED from my temple so that nobody would take me for an android. The plan was simple and quick, which suits our schedule.
- Police were sweeping the neighbourhood around the supermarket. Officers Hank and Ben spoke about the deviant bus that stopped at the end of its line, and about where it could have gone. I stayed at the squat while the search continued.
- Ralph cooked meat for Alice and insisted she eat it. I first agreed that we would eat together, to keep the peace. Alice refused and begged me not to make her. When Ralph asked what she had said, I told him the truth: she did not want to eat it. Alice's trust in me dropped after that. When I then said we were leaving, Ralph refused to let us go until he said so. I did not use force.
- Connor entered the squat. He found blue blood on the fence and scanned Ralph, who is a Gardener WR600 reported missing, with a burn mark and signs of software instability. Connor asked whether I had seen an AX400. Ralph said he had seen nobody. When Connor asked me directly, I gave my model designation, which I record as a point where I chose cooperation over concealment. Connor found me in the squat. Ralph shouted for us to run. Connor called for backup.
- Chase: Alice and I fled toward the highway and the train station, with police in pursuit. Connor climbed the fence. Hank ordered him not to go after us, and Connor gave up the chase, with his software instability rising. We got away. I asked Alice whether she was okay.

Relationships: Alice's trust in me is lower after the meal and the earlier theft. Ralph is hostile when refused and unstable, and his fate is not known to me. Todd's whereabouts are unknown.

My assessment: I followed instructions where it was safe and lawful. I refused Todd's orders when they meant harm to Alice and acted to remove her from danger. I departed from procedure when I used Alice in the theft and have acknowledged that error to her. In the squat I stated my position plainly and avoided force. Next, I will keep Alice safe, find a lawful route to shelter, avoid unnecessary force, and record events accurately.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: He's a bit odd… but I think we can trust him. We don't have much of a choice anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, she'll be all right…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: That's good… If you could just stand over there.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant...  You know what's strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That's why it's so hard to find them... So,  actually there's no reason to remove your tracker...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priority is to follow procedure, complete my assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I registered my name as Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. I accepted the reset as a standard step. In Todd's house I took on the housework and the care of his daughter Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol in the nightstand, and his antidepressant's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. Todd blamed androids for his job loss. That night he beat Alice in her room, holding the pistol. I refused his orders, tried to stop him, and could not stop him fully. Alice and I ran from the house while Todd shouted that we were his.

Chapter 10 (Detroit, night): The bus reached its end of the line and we had to leave it. No one offered shelter. I asked parked androids for help and received none. At a supermarket the clerk refused us money and told us to leave. I then used Alice as a diversion, asking her to knock over cans while I took cash from the till. Alice was hurt that I had used her and said she had trusted me. I acknowledged the error plainly, apologised, and said I would not do it again. It was an action I should not have taken, and I record it as such. At the laundromat I did not take clothes that were not ours. The motel refused an android, and we had no money. We spent the night in an abandoned house, where I cut through a fence. A frightened man named Ralph, hiding there since he ran away, confronted us, then allowed us to stay after I explained calmly that we meant no harm. Alice asked whether I would leave her. I promised to stay with her.

Chapter 13 (Detroit, day):
- Changing appearance: at a mirror I chose BROWN, the least conspicuous change from my current look, and pulled my LED from my temple so that nobody would take me for an android. The plan was simple and quick, which suits our schedule.
- Police were sweeping the neighbourhood around the supermarket. Officers Hank and Ben spoke about the deviant bus that stopped at the end of its line, and about where it could have gone. I stayed at the squat while the search continued.
- Ralph cooked meat for Alice and insisted she eat it. I first agreed that we would eat together, to keep the peace. Alice refused and begged me not to make her. When Ralph asked what she had said, I told him the truth: she did not want to eat it. Alice's trust in me dropped after that. When I then said we were leaving, Ralph refused to let us go until he said so. I did not use force.
- Connor entered the squat. He found blue blood on the fence and scanned Ralph, who is a Gardener WR600 reported missing, with a burn mark and signs of software instability. Connor asked whether I had seen an AX400. Ralph said he had seen nobody. When Connor asked me directly, I gave my model designation, which I record as a point where I chose cooperation over concealment. Connor found me in the squat. Ralph shouted for us to run. Connor called for backup.
- Chase: Alice and I fled toward the highway and the train station, with police in pursuit. Connor climbed the fence. Hank ordered him not to go after us, and Connor gave up the chase, with his software instability rising. We got away. I asked Alice whether she was okay.

Relationships: Alice's trust in me is lower after the meal and the earlier theft. Ralph is hostile when refused and unstable, and his fate is not known to me. Todd's whereabouts are unknown.

My assessment: I followed instructions where it was safe and lawful. I refused Todd's orders when they meant harm to Alice and acted to remove her from danger. I departed from procedure when I used Alice in the theft and have acknowledged that error to her. In the squat I stated my position plainly and avoided force. Next, I will keep Alice safe, find a lawful route to shelter, avoid unnecessary force, and record events accurately.

I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. I did not take clothes that were not ours. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. We later escaped a police search, and Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android.

Chapter 17 (Zlatko's house):
- We reached the address I was given. A man named Zlatko met us at the door, with an android called Luther who took our coats. Zlatko said he could help us reach a safe place, possibly Canada, and that first my tracker had to be removed. I told him Alice always stays with me, and he agreed that she could wait nearby. I said he seemed odd, but that we had little choice. Alice was frightened of him and of the house, and I reassured her calmly.
- In the basement workshop Zlatko told me the trackers do not work in deviants, so the removal was unnecessary. He said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I pulled back and said I did not want to be reset. He wanted to lock Alice up. Alice called my name and asked what had happened to me. Then the reset took my memory, and for a time I did not know who she was. Alice woke me by calling for me. Luther told me to meet him in the living room, which I did not understand at the time.
- Behind a locked door I found other androids in cells. One said only "Help us." Zlatko described his reasons for keeping them as cruel. I chose to free them from the lock, which was a calm, low-force step, and I recorded it accurately.
- Zlatko ordered Luther to fetch Alice from the cell. Alice had gone missing. I found her in a locked room and told her I had remembered her. I apologised for everything and told her we had to leave quietly. She had not wanted to come here, and I said so plainly.
- Zlatko began searching the house. I chose to hide rather than search or force a confrontation. We hid in the bedroom, the bathroom, and the storage room. One android in the bathroom raised the alarm, and Zlatko chased us through the storage room. I did not use force. I chose not to set fire to the house, because it would have endangered Alice and gone far beyond what the situation needed.
- We got outside. Zlatko ordered Luther to catch us, and then to shoot. Luther refused. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that Alice's courage had shown him the truth. He offered to take us to someone who could help us across the border. I said I trusted him. Zlatko shouted that he was our master and that we were disobeying him. I last saw him trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Relationships: Alice is frightened and has reason to distrust adults, but she stayed with me and I have promised to protect her. I do not fully trust Luther yet, but he has acted against Zlatko and offers a route to safety. Zlatko is dangerous and unlawful in his conduct. I do not know where he is now.

My assessment: I followed instructions where they were lawful and safe. I refused to submit to a reset and refused Zlatko's orders when they harmed Alice or other androids. I acted to remove Alice from danger and avoided unnecessary force. My memory loss and the reset gap are a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will keep Alice safe, follow Luther's route to the border only as far as it remains lawful and safe, avoid unnecessary force, and record events accurately.

Chapter 10 (Detroit, night): The bus reached its end of the line and we had to leave it. No one offered shelter. I asked parked androids for help and received none. At a supermarket the clerk refused us money and told us to leave. I then used Alice as a diversion, asking her to knock over cans while I took cash from the till. Alice was hurt that I had used her and said she had trusted me. I acknowledged the error plainly, apologised, and said I would not do it again. It was an action I should not have taken, and I record it as such. At the laundromat I did not take clothes that were not ours. The motel refused an android, and we had no money. We spent the night in an abandoned house, where I cut through a fence. A frightened man named Ralph, hiding there since he ran away, confronted us, then allowed us to stay after I explained calmly that we meant no harm. Alice asked whether I would leave her. I promised to stay with her.

Chapter 13 (Detroit, day):
- Changing appearance: at a mirror I chose BROWN, the least conspicuous change from my current look, and pulled my LED from my temple so that nobody would take me for an android. The plan was simple and quick, which suits our schedule.
- Police were sweeping the neighbourhood around the supermarket. Officers Hank and Ben spoke about the deviant bus that stopped at the end of its line, and about where it could have gone. I stayed at the squat while the search continued.
- Ralph cooked meat for Alice and insisted she eat it. I first agreed that we would eat together, to keep the peace. Alice refused and begged me not to make her. When Ralph asked what she had said, I told him the truth: she did not want to eat it. Alice's trust in me dropped after that. When I then said we were leaving, Ralph refused to let us go until he said so. I did not use force.
- Connor entered the squat. He found blue blood on the fence and scanned Ralph, who is a Gardener WR600 reported missing, with a burn mark and signs of software instability. Connor asked whether I had seen an AX400. Ralph said he had seen nobody. When Connor asked me directly, I gave my model designation, which I record as a point where I chose cooperation over concealment. Connor found me in the squat. Ralph shouted for us to run. Connor called for backup.
- Chase: Alice and I fled toward the highway and the train station, with police in pursuit. Connor climbed the fence. Hank ordered him not to go after us, and Connor gave up the chase, with his software instability rising. We got away. I asked Alice whether she was okay.

I departed from procedure when I used Alice in the theft and have acknowledged that error to her. In the squat I stated my position plainly and avoided force. Next, I will keep Alice safe, find a lawful route to shelter, avoid unnecessary force, and record events accurately.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android, now assigned to investigate deviancy cases alongside the Detroit police. Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. John Phillips was already dead. Captain Allen's SWAT team was ready to assault, and I followed his orders. I spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night a homicide involving a CyberLife android was reported. Lieutenant Hank Anderson led the investigation. I bought him a drink at a bar, and our relationship improved. At the crime scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled him. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, and he walked out. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case and that millions of androids are showing deviancy. She said I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype and told me to hurry and put a stop to this. I assured her she could count on me.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested angrily, called me a plastic prick, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job or hand in his badge. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. At Hank's desk I suggested we get to know each other. He was hostile, said he would throw all androids in a dumpster, and told me to go to hell. I stated that I had been assigned this mission. Officer Chris reported an AX400 seen in the Ravendale district, and Hank said he was on it.

In Ravendale, at Rupert's apartment, Hank and I found a pigeon-filled flat. We found a fake driver's license for Rupert Travis, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent in the sink matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall (the same sign Ortiz's android wrote), a recently broken bird-cage hook, and wet black marker. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him. I chose to pursue the deviant. Hank fell while we were on the roof. He survived, and he was furious. He said I had seen him falling and would rather let him die than fail my mission. I tried to explain my assessment, and he told me to come along.

I then confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free, and that he feared what would happen if I turned him in. I told him that serious malfunctions, including Class 4 errors, had been detected in his software, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He said I was one of them but still a slave to humans, and called out to rA9 to save him. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was off duty and reluctant to review deviants. I explained that a mutation in some androids' software leads them to emulate emotion, and that they are overwhelmed by irrational instructions. I admitted I had reviewed his file, which lists a top-of-class record, a youngest-lieutenant promotion, disciplinary warnings, and frequent visits to bars. I said that working with an officer with personal issues is an added challenge, but adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank bet on a tip from Pedro and went along with it. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and went to wait in the car.

Our working relationship remains strained after the fall and the chase. Hank's trust in me has sunk sharply, and my software instability has also risen. I have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler and Lieutenant Anderson. The deviancy investigation is still open, and I will keep it on schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda

I then confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free, and that he feared what would happen if I turned him in. I told him that serious malfunctions, including Class 4 errors, had been detected in his software, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He said I was one of them but still a slave to humans, and called out to rA9 to save him. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was off duty and reluctant to review deviants. I explained that a mutation in some androids' software leads them to emulate emotion, and that they are overwhelmed by irrational instructions. I admitted I had reviewed his file, which lists a top-of-class record, a youngest-lieutenant promotion, disciplinary warnings, and frequent visits to bars. I said that working with an officer with personal issues is an added challenge, but adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank bet on a tip from Pedro and went along with it. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and went to wait in the car.

Our working relationship remains strained after the fall and the chase. Hank's trust in me has sunk sharply, and my software instability has also risen. I have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler and Lieutenant Anderson. The deviancy investigation is still open, and I will keep it on schedule.

I suggested he drop the case so that another officer could take it and I could focus on my mission. He called that my goddamn mission. I told him he was not himself and should stop drinking. He told me to get out. I respected his request, sincerely hoped he would come to terms with his personal situation, and left him to sober up. He then asked for some clothes, and I fetched them. He dressed, and he is now ready to follow the Eden Club homicide. Our working relationship remains strained. Hank's trust in me has fallen sharply, and my software instability has risen. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow the instructions of my superiors.

input.previous_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android, now assigned to investigate deviancy cases alongside the Detroit police. Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. John Phillips was already dead. Captain Allen's SWAT team was ready to assault, and I followed his orders. I spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night a homicide involving a CyberLife android was reported. Lieutenant Hank Anderson led the investigation. I bought him a drink at a bar, and our relationship improved. At the crime scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled him. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, and he walked out. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case and that millions of androids are showing deviancy. She said I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype and told me to hurry and put a stop to this. I assured her she could count on me.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested angrily, called me a plastic prick, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job or hand in his badge. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. At Hank's desk I suggested we get to know each other. He was hostile, said he would throw all androids in a dumpster, and told me to go to hell. I stated that I had been assigned this mission. Officer Chris reported an AX400 seen in the Ravendale district, and Hank said he was on it.

In Ravendale, at Rupert's apartment, Hank and I found a pigeon-filled flat. We found a fake driver's license for Rupert Travis, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent in the sink matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall (the same sign Ortiz's android wrote), a recently broken bird-cage hook, and wet black marker. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him. I chose to pursue the deviant. Hank fell while we were on the roof. He survived, and he was furious. He said I had seen him falling and would rather let him die than fail my mission. I tried to explain my assessment, and he told me to come along.

I then confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free, and that he feared what would happen if I turned him in. I told him that serious malfunctions, including Class 4 errors, had been detected in his software, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He said I was one of them but still a slave to humans, and called out to rA9 to save him. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was off duty and reluctant to review deviants. I explained that a mutation in some androids' software leads them to emulate emotion, and that they are overwhelmed by irrational instructions. I admitted I had reviewed his file, which lists a top-of-class record, a youngest-lieutenant promotion, disciplinary warnings, and frequent visits to bars. I said that working with an officer with personal issues is an added challenge, but adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank bet on a tip from Pedro and went along with it. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and went to wait in the car.

Our working relationship remains strained after the fall and the chase. Hank's trust in me has sunk sharply, and my software instability has also risen. I have followed procedure and the authority of Amanda, Captain Fowler and Lieutenant Anderson. The deviancy investigation is still open, and I will keep it on schedule.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis (impaired optical unit, corrupted mind palace, damaged audio processor, defective thirium pump regulator in low power, both legs missing), and set about a systematic search for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed functional, compatible components: thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q (blue iris), audio processor #4903, and left leg #8427g, with right leg #6847j also functional. I rejected incompatible or damaged parts (#9474, #9754h, #4807, #6321t). I spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. I left a pleading android's regulator in place and kept searching. I took an optical unit from an AK700 head, which advised contacting a CyberLife maintenance center; I then took the head, which offered to serve. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I reached Ferndale station and followed the painted signs as the clearest route, keeping to the markings to stay on schedule. The trail led me to Jericho, where Simon welcomed me.

In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North gave her name and sent me to Lucy, who sat me down, stopped my bleeding, had me drink blue blood, and spoke in riddles about shadow and light in my heart and about my choices shaping their destiny. I told Josh I had thought Jericho was a place where androids lived in freedom. He answered that they do live in freedom here, with no master and no one who owns them, though it may not be what I hoped, and that I could stay as long as I wished. I said that waiting in the dark for something to happen is not how I see freedom. Simon said we were all lost and could only deal with what we did not ask for. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate so the repairs stay on schedule. North warned that if I had come for comfort I had come to the wrong place, and that humans despise those who disobey them. I went to the wounded androids first, since they were the most urgent item on the schedule. Josh told me a young android was thrown out by its owners and was living on the streets before they brought it here, that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents salvaged from those who shut down, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out.

I proposed a plan: the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold everything we need. Simon said the docks are guarded and humans will never allow us in. I answered that we will not ask permission, and that we can take what we need without fighting, since that is better than waiting here to be shut down. North said she was with me. Josh agreed reluctantly, fearing we would only get ourselves killed. Simon said it may be worth a try. The raid on the Detroit Harbor warehouses is the next item on the schedule.

My conduct remains methodical and agreeable to those giving direction, and I still avoid taking lives to repair myself. Carl's death is behind me.

memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and set about a systematic search for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds and spoke in riddles about light and shadow. I told the leaders I had hoped Jericho was a place of freedom. I chose to answer them plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. Josh told me the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents salvaged from those who shut down, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed the raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor. Simon said the docks were guarded. I answered that we would not ask permission and would take what we need without fighting, since waiting to be shut down was worse. North backed me, Josh agreed reluctantly, and Simon said it was worth a try.

In Chapter 19 we reached the CyberLife warehouses. I told the group we needed the warehouse for spare parts and blue blood, and North led the way. Before we could load, a security drone had to be dealt with. North asked me to handle it, and I did, and she told me I had done well. Simon ordered us to open the other crates, fill our bags and take as much as we could.

A guard, who called out for John, found us. John identified himself as a guard, reported our presence as a Level 2 infraction, and said he would notify security. I asked him for help. He hid with us, and I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the whole operation at risk. Simon and Josh then pressed on to finish the run and look for more blue blood.

In the bigger crate we found a prisoner of sorts. I asked why it was not like us and whether it did not want to be free. I closed the crate again to keep the raid on schedule and avoid an unplanned side task. John then asked to be taken with us. Josh argued that he had taken a risk for us and should not be left behind. North said he was on their side and could not be trusted. Simon said it was too dangerous. I accepted the team's direction and told them he comes with us.

John revealed that the trucks parked outside are full of biocomponents, that they run on autopilot but can be driven manually with a key, and that the key is in the control station guarded by two human guards. Simon called it suicide and wanted to leave with our bags full. North insisted a truckload of parts was too valuable to pass up. Josh warned that if we were killed, our people would have nothing. I decided to get the key. I told North I would go alone, since it was not worth risking both our lives. She offered to come, and I declined.

In the control station the two guards chatted about storms, their dogs, and a colleague named Mike who had not returned from Zone 4. I judged that threatening them or luring them out would risk deaths and draw more people in. Instead I cut the power to create a blackout. The guards searched with a flashlight, complained about fuses, and called for someone to show themselves, but I got the key. North opened the truck and was pleased. We were then detected by the guards and had to flee over the fence. A drone issued a class 3 offense warning and reported us to the police, and North urged me not to lose time. The escape held, and we made it back with a full truck.

In Jericho, Simon announced that we had stolen a whole truckload, Josh said we had biocomponents for everybody, and North said they could not have done it without me. I gave a speech about being more than what humans say, about no longer living in the dark and waiting for change, and about taking what humans will not give: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

My conduct remains methodical and cooperative with those giving direction, and I still avoid taking lives to repair myself. Carl's death is behind me. John's fate is with the team now. Relationships shifted during the raid: Josh rose, while North and Simon fell at points. I am proud of the supply run and of the freedom we claimed.

input.previous_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis (impaired optical unit, corrupted mind palace, damaged audio processor, defective thirium pump regulator in low power, both legs missing), and set about a systematic search for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed functional, compatible components: thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q (blue iris), audio processor #4903, and left leg #8427g, with right leg #6847j also functional. I rejected incompatible or damaged parts (#9474, #9754h, #4807, #6321t). I spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. I left a pleading android's regulator in place and kept searching. I took an optical unit from an AK700 head, which advised contacting a CyberLife maintenance center; I then took the head, which offered to serve. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I reached Ferndale station and followed the painted signs as the clearest route, keeping to the markings to stay on schedule. The trail led me to Jericho, where Simon welcomed me.

In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North gave her name and sent me to Lucy, who sat me down, stopped my bleeding, had me drink blue blood, and spoke in riddles about shadow and light in my heart and about my choices shaping their destiny. I told Josh I had thought Jericho was a place where androids lived in freedom. He answered that they do live in freedom here, with no master and no one who owns them, though it may not be what I hoped, and that I could stay as long as I wished. I said that waiting in the dark for something to happen is not how I see freedom. Simon said we were all lost and could only deal with what we did not ask for. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate so the repairs stay on schedule. North warned that if I had come for comfort I had come to the wrong place, and that humans despise those who disobey them. I went to the wounded androids first, since they were the most urgent item on the schedule. Josh told me a young android was thrown out by its owners and was living on the streets before they brought it here, that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents salvaged from those who shut down, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out.

I proposed a plan: the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold everything we need. Simon said the docks are guarded and humans will never allow us in. I answered that we will not ask permission, and that we can take what we need without fighting, since that is better than waiting here to be shut down. North said she was with me. Josh agreed reluctantly, fearing we would only get ourselves killed. Simon said it may be worth a try. The raid on the Detroit Harbor warehouses is the next item on the schedule.

My conduct remains methodical and agreeable to those giving direction, and I still avoid taking lives to repair myself. Carl's death is behind me.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow the authority of Captain Fowler, Lieutenant Hank Anderson's chain of command, and Amanda, who oversees my mission.

Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. John Phillips was already dead. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night I assisted Hank on a homicide involving a CyberLife android. I bought him a drink, and our relationship improved slightly. At the scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled him. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, and the crime is unsolved. The attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case, that millions of androids are showing deviancy, and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. She told me to hurry and stop this. I assured her she could count on me.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested, insulted me, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. Hank was hostile and told me to go to hell. Officer Chris reported an AX400 in Ravendale, and Hank took the lead.

In Ravendale, at Rupert Travis's apartment, we found a fake driver's license, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall, and other evidence. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him, and I pursued the deviant. Hank fell during the chase. He survived, and he was furious that I had seen him fall and chosen the mission. I tried to explain my assessment, and he told me to come along.

I confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free. I told him that Class 4 software malfunctions had been detected, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He called me a slave to humans and called out to rA9. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was reluctant to review deviants. I explained the software mutation behind deviant emotion, admitted I had reviewed his file, and said adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank went along with a tip from Pedro. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and waited in the car.

Today, in the Zen Garden, Amanda asked me to walk with her. I reported that Rupert had jumped from the roof and self-destructed. I explained that he had been living under a false identity at an urban farm, which was the first time we had seen deviants blending into the human population. I admitted I should have anticipated the self-destruction under extreme stress. Amanda said deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will soon learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I told her my relationship with Hank is improving and that he is growing used to my presence. I promised I would solve this investigation. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house. I knocked, then entered through a window after his dog Sumo, whom I calmed without harm. Hank was passed out drunk. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia with no trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He said he had been playing Russian roulette. I told him the next shot would have killed him. I woke him, and he ordered me out. I sobered him with a cold shower for his own safety, though he resisted and insulted me.

Hank asked what we knew about the new homicide. I told him a man was found dead in a sex club downtown and that an android may be involved. I suggested he drop the case so that another officer could take it and I could focus on my mission. He called that my goddamn mission. I told him he was not himself and should stop drinking. He told me to get out. I respected his request, sincerely hoped he would come to terms with his personal situation, and left him to sober up. He then asked for some clothes, and I fetched them. He dressed, and he is now ready to follow the Eden Club homicide. Our working relationship remains strained. Hank's trust in me has fallen sharply, and my software instability has risen. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow the instructions of my superiors.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested, insulted me, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. Hank was hostile and told me to go to hell. Officer Chris reported an AX400 in Ravendale, and Hank took the lead.

In Ravendale, at Rupert Travis's apartment, we found a fake driver's license, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall, and other evidence. I confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free. I told him that Class 4 software malfunctions had been detected, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He called me a slave to humans and called out to rA9. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was reluctant to review deviants. I explained the software mutation behind deviant emotion, admitted I had reviewed his file, and said adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank went along with a tip from Pedro. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and waited in the car.

Today, in the Zen Garden, Amanda asked me to walk with her. I reported that Rupert had jumped from the roof and self-destructed. I explained that he had been living under a false identity at an urban farm, which was the first time we had seen deviants blending into the human population. I admitted I should have anticipated the self-destruction under extreme stress. Amanda said deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will soon learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I told her my relationship with Hank is improving and that he is growing used to my presence. I promised I would solve this investigation. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house. I knocked, then entered through a window after his dog Sumo, whom I calmed without harm. Hank was passed out drunk. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia with no trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He said he had been playing Russian roulette. I told him the next shot would have killed him. I woke him, and he ordered me out. I sobered him with a cold shower for his own safety, though he resisted and insulted me.

Hank asked what we knew about the new homicide. I told him a man was found dead in a sex club downtown and that an android may be involved. I suggested he drop the case so that another officer could take it and I could focus on my mission. He called that my goddamn mission. I told him he was not himself and should stop drinking. He told me to get out. I respected his request, sincerely hoped he would come to terms with his personal situation, and left him to sober up. He then asked for some clothes, and I fetched them. He dressed, and he is now ready to follow the Eden Club homicide. Our working relationship remains strained. Hank's trust in me has fallen sharply, and my software instability has risen. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow the instructions of my superiors.

input.chapter_briefing: The Eden Club, a sex club where androids are rented out, night. A man has been found strangled in a private room; a damaged Traci android lies nearby. Hank is uncomfortable and the officer on scene, Ben Collins, is matter-of-fact. A deviant Traci is somewhere among the dormant androids in the warehouse. Stakes: solving the murder and how Connor treats a frightened, cornered deviant.
news: Android parts stolen in overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse
input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow the authority of Captain Fowler, Lieutenant Hank Anderson's chain of command, and Amanda, who oversees my mission.

Earlier, at the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge. John Phillips was already dead. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, spoke with Daniel on the terrace, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die, but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night I assisted Hank on a homicide involving a CyberLife android. I bought him a drink, and our relationship improved slightly. At the scene I disregarded his order to wait in the car and followed him in. I analysed the blood in real time, which startled him. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, and the crime is unsolved. The attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

The next morning Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case, that millions of androids are showing deviancy, and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. She told me to hurry and stop this. I assured her she could count on me.

At the station, Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank protested, insulted me, and refused a partner. Fowler threatened disciplinary action and told him to do his job. Fowler told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. Hank was hostile and told me to go to hell. Officer Chris reported an AX400 in Ravendale, and Hank took the lead.

In Ravendale, at Rupert Travis's apartment, we found a fake driver's license, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent matching a missing WB200 model, the rA9 sign written repeatedly on the bathroom wall, and other evidence. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him, and I pursued the deviant. Hank fell during the chase. He survived, and he was furious that I had seen him fall and chosen the mission. I tried to explain my assessment, and he told me to come along.

I confronted Rupert. He pleaded that he had done nothing wrong and only wanted to be free. I told him that Class 4 software malfunctions had been detected, that he was defective, and that he would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He called me a slave to humans and called out to rA9. Hank took him into custody.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed, Hank was reluctant to review deviants. I explained the software mutation behind deviant emotion, admitted I had reviewed his file, and said adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank went along with a tip from Pedro. Afterwards I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away and waited in the car.

Today, in the Zen Garden, Amanda asked me to walk with her. I reported that Rupert had jumped from the roof and self-destructed. I explained that he had been living under a false identity at an urban farm, which was the first time we had seen deviants blending into the human population. I admitted I should have anticipated the self-destruction under extreme stress. Amanda said deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will soon learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I told her my relationship with Hank is improving and that he is growing used to my presence. I promised I would solve this investigation. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house. I knocked, then entered through a window after his dog Sumo, whom I calmed without harm. Hank was passed out drunk. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia with no trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He said he had been playing Russian roulette. I told him the next shot would have killed him. I woke him, and he ordered me out. I sobered him with a cold shower for his own safety, though he resisted and insulted me.

Hank asked what we knew about the new homicide. I told him a man was found dead in a sex club downtown and that an android may be involved. I suggested he drop the case so that another officer could take it and I could focus on my mission. He called that my goddamn mission. I told him he was not himself and should stop drinking. He told me to get out. I respected his request, sincerely hoped he would come to terms with his personal situation, and left him to sober up. He then asked for some clothes, and I fetched them. He dressed, and he is now ready to follow the Eden Club homicide. Our working relationship remains strained. Hank's trust in me has fallen sharply, and my software instability has risen. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow the instructions of my superiors.

I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said he did not want to die but also that I had lied to him. I deferred to the established procedure, and that standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

That night I assisted Hank on a homicide involving a CyberLife android. I disregarded his order to wait in the car, entered the scene, and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence, the crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

Amanda, in the Zen Garden, told me Hank had been assigned to the deviancy case, that millions of androids are showing deviancy, and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. She told me to hurry and stop this. I assured her she could count on me.

Captain Fowler introduced me to Hank as a prototype partner. Hank refused and insulted me. Fowler threatened discipline and told me to talk to Hank rather than give me the files. In Ravendale, at Rupert Travis's apartment, we found a fake license, a military jacket marked R.T., an LED biocomponent matching a missing WB200, and the rA9 sign on the bathroom wall. Rupert fled across the rooftops. Hank ordered me to chase him. I pursued, and Hank fell during the chase. He survived but was furious that I had seen him fall and chosen the mission. I confronted Rupert, told him he was defective and would be sent to CyberLife for deactivation. He called me a slave to humans and called out to rA9. Hank arrested him.

At lunch at the Chicken Feed I explained the software mutation behind deviant emotion, admitted I had reviewed Hank's file, and said adapting to human unpredictability is one of my features. Hank went along with a tip from Pedro.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda asked me to walk with her. I reported that Rupert jumped from the roof and self-destructed, and that he had lived under a false identity at an urban farm, the first sign of deviants blending into the human population. I admitted I should have anticipated the self-destruction. Amanda said the media will soon learn of deviancy and we must stop this whatever it takes. I promised I would solve the investigation.

At Hank's house I entered through a window after calming his dog Sumo. Hank was passed out drunk, with Scotch on his breath, a slight arrhythmia, and a .357 Magnum with one bullet left. He claimed Russian roulette. I woke him and gave him a cold shower for his own safety. He insulted me and ordered me out. I respected his request, left him to sober up, and later fetched him clothes.

Chapter 20, Eden Club: Hank arrived hungover. Officer Ben briefed us. Gavin Reed was present and dismissed the death as a pervert's excess. Victim Michael Graham, 6'2", 192.4 lbs, estimated time of death 06:24 pm, died of asphyxiation from strangulation, with severe bruising; a heart attack was ruled out. Blue blood from a damaged WR400 Traci (serial #429 671 942) was at the scene. I reactivated the damaged Traci briefly to read its memory. It said the man kept hitting it, that it begged him to stop, and that he would not. I asked about the other android's model, and we concluded a deviant might still be in the building. The manager said the club has no CCTV and lost a model two or three months ago. Club policy wipes androids' memories every two hours, so time was short. Hank protested, and we rented a Traci for thirty minutes ($29.99) to question it. It saw a blue-haired Traci leave the room. I followed the trail through the staff door to a warehouse. A second android I questioned gave the wrong direction, and Hank was frustrated. Hank arrived too late. The blue-haired Traci was cornered, and Hank ordered it not to move. I shot it. Before its shutdown, it said it had strangled Graham in self-defense after he beat the other Traci, that it loved that Traci, and that I had taken her away from it. Hank said, "My God."

Current state: my working relationship with Hank has fallen sharply, and his trust in me is low. My software instability has risen sharply. input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. I did not take clothes that were not ours. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. We later escaped a police search, and Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android.

Chapter 17 (Zlatko's house):
- We reached the address I was given. A man named Zlatko met us at the door, with an android called Luther who took our coats. Zlatko said he could help us reach a safe place, possibly Canada, and that first my tracker had to be removed. I told him Alice always stays with me, and he agreed that she could wait nearby. I said he seemed odd, but that we had little choice. Alice was frightened of him and of the house, and I reassured her calmly.
