input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.

I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft. I acknowledged that error plainly to her and apologised. We stayed in an abandoned house with Ralph, a Gardener WR600 who was hostile when refused. Connor let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED so I would not be taken for an android. At Zlatko's house, Zlatko claimed he reset deviants and sold them or used them for experiments. I refused a reset, and my memory was wiped for a time. I freed the caged androids from a locked room, using calm, low-force means, and recorded it accurately. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him, and I did not set fire to the house. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I last saw Zlatko trying to stop Luther. I do not know what happened to him.

Chapter 21 (the road north):
- In the car, Luther and I discussed the people we were going to meet. Luther had overheard that Zlatko had captured androids who were being helped across the border by humans. I said that might be a lie or another trap. Luther said the androids he overheard believed it, until Zlatko killed them. I noted both possibilities and kept the plan as agreed.
- The radio reported that the AX400 from a Detroit suburb is still at large, and that the Arctic conflict is escalating, with a US submarine missing. The forecast was 22 degrees with heavy snow.
- The car broke down and the emergency brakes engaged. The temperature was about 30 degrees below freezing, and Alice was ill. I told her to stay inside. Luther suggested continuing on foot. I judged that Alice would not survive the night outside and that we needed shelter. Alice was the priority.
- We found Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I checked the nearby buildings with Luther. None was suitable, so we settled in the tavern. Luther made a fire in a safe position so we would not be smoked out. I offered Alice cookies. She declined because she was not hungry. I made her a bed.
- Alice asked whether we would ever be like the people on the old poster. I gave her a realistic answer: we would not be like them, but we could build a happy life in our own way once we crossed the border. I told her a bedtime story. I did not promise a happy ending, and I told her it was up to us to write the end. Alice said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I also told Luther goodnight on Alice's behalf.
- Luther asked whether I had noticed anything about Alice that was different. I asked him to explain before I answered. I have not yet heard what he meant. He said he had not thought about life after the border, and that he did not yet know what being free meant.
- At midnight Alice screamed for me. Shapes were outside the tavern. I chose to ask who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, an android who had worked at the park before it closed, said they had wanted to see who was there because humans sometimes came to hurt them. Jerry offered Alice a carousel ride. I said she was tired and that we would be leaving tomorrow. Luther said we had no choice. Alice smiled for the first time I had seen. Hunters then arrived. I do not know what happened next.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Luther is steadily more loyal and has acted against Zlatko. I still do not know what he meant about Alice. Jerry and the other park androids are unknown and I have not verified them. Hunters are now a threat.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe. I chose shelter for Alice over continuing in the cold, and I questioned strangers before acting. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. Next, I will protect Alice, verify the threat from the hunters, keep Alice warm and close, and clarify Luther's observation about her.

I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko.

Chapter 21 (the road north): The car broke down in severe cold. Alice was ill, so I judged shelter to be the priority over walking on. We settled in the tavern at Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I made Alice a bed and told her a bedtime story, without promising a happy ending. Luther asked whether I had noticed something different about Alice. I asked him to explain first. I have not yet heard what he meant. At midnight, shapes were outside. I asked who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, a park android, offered Alice a carousel ride. I declined on the grounds that she was tired. Hunters then arrived.

Chapter 25 (Rose's house): Rose and her son Adam took us in after I asked for help at their door. Luther asked whether we could trust them. I judged that we had no real alternative and went in on the agreed route. Alice was running a fever. Rose prepared a meal and medicine, and I asked Alice to eat. I told Alice that these people would help us and that we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise, and I have recorded it as an overstatement. Rose said the river crossing was risky and that staying put was safer for now. I pressed for help crossing, and she then said we would leave that night.

In the storage room, an android named Mary had shut down. Her companions were grieving, and I left them alone. Adam was hostile. He said androids were nothing and that his father's death was the cause of these troubles. Rose sent him out of the room and said she would arrange the crossing.

Police arrived. I asked Adam to stay calm. I opened the door and offered the officer coffee. When he asked about other people in the house, I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. That was true of Alice, but I did not mention Luther. When asked about androids, I said they had worked in the garden and that the android in the locker belonged to a previous tenant. Both answers were incomplete and the second was false. I should have answered plainly. The officer found Luther. Luther told Alice and me that we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. Adam said the police had killed him. I did not see the full sequence and I cannot confirm his fate. Rose then told us to get ready, because we were leaving that night.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe, and I chose shelter for Alice over exposure. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. However, I gave the officer misleading answers, and I made a promise about Canada that I could not guarantee. I will correct those records where I can. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. I still do not know what Luther meant about Alice.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Rose is our host and has arranged the departure. I have not verified her motives or her plan. Adam is hostile and may expose us. Luther's fate is unclear and I hold his words about family. Jerry and the park androids are unverified. Hunters and police are now active threats.

Next: keep Alice warm, fed and close, keep to Rose's departure arrangement while verifying it where I can, and watch for further danger. I will correct my account to the police if the opportunity arises and clarify Luther's observation about Alice.

dialogue.text: What's going on?

dialogue.text: It's Mary.  She just shut down…

dialogue.text: We escaped together…  We used to talk about what we would do once we got across the border…  I loved her.  I loved her more than anything.  What would I do without her?..

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Let's let them be…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice? What are you doing here? You should be resting…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I wasn't sleepy…

chapter_segment.rationale: Rose, our authorised host, advised that staying hidden is safer until conditions settle, and Alice is running a fever and needs rest. Keeping her inside follows the hosts' arrangements and avoids an unplanned move into the open.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Come on, Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: She didn't wanna stay in her room any longer… You alright, Kara?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes...  I'm fine.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: We can't hide them! Not after what those deviants did today! It's too dangerous! Do you know what'll happen if the police find them here? We'll go to prison, Mom! Do you understand me? Prison!

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Adam, we’ve already talked about this!

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: No! I won't back down this time! You're gonna ruin our lives, and for what? For a bunch of machines?

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: They're not machines! They're alive!

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: I'm alive! You are alive! They!.. They're nothing! And none of this would be happening if dad was still here!

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: I will not stand for that kind of talk!

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: I'm not going to prison because you wanna help these freaks!

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: THAT IS ENOUGH ADAM! THAT'S ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Don’t mind him… Sometimes he just boils over… It’s been hard since his dad passed away… But he's a fine boy!.. I'll go see about getting you across the border tonight, okay?.. You stay here, I won't be long.

chapter_segment.rationale: Rose is our authorised host and has said she will arrange the border crossing tonight, so I will stay where I was asked and wait for her return. This keeps Alice resting and the handover on schedule without moving around the house unnecessarily.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: The police!.. It's the police!

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: What are we gonna do? They know we're here!  We have to open the door! I knew this was gonna happen! I knew it!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Hurry, Luther! Take Alice and hide…

chapter_segment.rationale: Rose assigned the spare room upstairs for Alice's bed, and following our host's arrangement keeps the handover orderly and gets Alice resting for her fever. Going up now also keeps us on schedule for the border crossing.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …upstairs!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Come on, Alice!

chapter_segment.rationale: Adam is agitated and the police are at the door, so a calm, polite response is the most orderly way to keep the situation under control and protect Alice. It also avoids escalating the confrontation and keeps our hosts cooperative.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: If they see you panicking, it’s over. Do you want to get us into trouble? Do you wanna get your mother into trouble? Then keep calm, and just do what I say...

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Good evening, Ma'am. Sorry to disturb you. We've had reports of androids in the area.  With all this deviant business going on, you can’t be too careful. Do you mind if I ask you a few questions? May I come in?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: 'Evening, young man.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: Good evening…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Would you like a cup of coffee?

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: I'd love one. Have you noticed anything unusual recently? Any unexpected visitors?

chapter_segment.rationale: I offered the officer coffee, and accepting his request keeps the interview moving on schedule while I stay polite and cooperative. Making it in the kitchen also gives me a calm, procedural task that lets me keep Alice and Adam's situation steady without escalating.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, nothing in particular…

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Is anyone else in the house?

chapter_segment.rationale: The officer asked directly whether anyone else is in the house, and I will answer truthfully and calmly rather than obstruct a lawful inquiry. Cooperating in this way keeps the interaction orderly and avoids giving the officer grounds to escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: There's… There's my daughter… She's asleep upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Do you have any androids here?

chapter_segment.rationale: The officer is conducting a lawful inquiry, and my procedure is to answer accurately rather than obstruct it, as I did with his previous question. A truthful answer keeps the interaction orderly and lets me manage the next steps calmly to protect Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We used to for… helping in the garden… but we got rid of it.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: What's with the blue blood? I thought you didn't have any androids?

chapter_segment.rationale: The officer is conducting a lawful inquiry, so a factual, cooperative answer keeps the interaction orderly. Identifying the android's previous owner gives him accurate records to work from while avoiding obstruction.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I-It belonged to the… The previous tenant…  I- I still haven't cleared all that out yet.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Hm, your daughter seems to have woken up.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: What's your name, son?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: Adam… M-my name is Adam…

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Is everything all right, Adam?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: The… The androids, they…

chapter_segment.rationale: The officer is conducting a lawful inquiry, so a calm, cooperative reply keeps the exchange orderly and avoids giving him grounds to escalate. A measured tone also helps protect Alice and keeps our hosts from being pulled into a larger confrontation.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: He needs a rest. He's been working in the garden all day…

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Do you know anything about deviants? Have you seen any?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: No… No… I-I haven't seen anything…

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: I better go. Thanks for the coffee.  Have a nice evening.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Is somebody else in the house?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: A draft… It must be a draft, I probably left a window open somewhere?..

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: Step aside ma'am. Oh shit! Don't move! In there, with them!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: He's dead!  You killed him!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: LUTHER!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: You're gonna have to finish the journey without me… I was just a machine. You made me part of a family…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Luther, no…

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.text: I don't believe this...  This is a nightmare...  This is a fucking nightmare!..

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. Josh explained that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, and North, Josh and Simon agreed to try.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us, reported a Level 2 infraction, and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I asked why the prisoner in the bigger crate was not free and closed the crate again to keep to schedule. John asked to come with us. Josh and North argued for and against him, Simon called it too dangerous, and I accepted the team's direction that he comes with us. John revealed the trucks outside are full of biocomponents and can be driven manually with a key held by two guards. I took the task of getting the key alone, judging it not worth risking two lives. In the control station I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, and I got the key. We were detected and fled over the fence with a full truck. In Jericho I gave a speech: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we returned to Jericho to broadcast our message to humans. Josh warned that revealing ourselves would put us in danger, Simon doubted anyone would listen, and North asked what we wanted. I told them that if we want freedom we must have the courage to ask for it, and that the operation must be planned to the smallest detail. Channel 16 broadcasts from Stratford Tower, and its control room is on the top floor.

At the tower's reception I asked for an appointment with Mr. Peterson. When asked for ID, I requested help, and the receptionist directed us to the elevators past the security gate. Two guards in the lobby talked of poker and of a colleague named Mike. To get past the desk, I phoned the desk manager, Elizabeth Wilson, with a false report of damage to her car in the car park, which drew her down to the garage. I noted her family and home details and chose not to use them, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. Going up, a cleaner android's trolley blocked the server room on floor 79, and two guards were puzzled by the malfunctioning machines. I asked a cleaner android for help, and it joined our cause. In the server room North took the platform and I took the window, and we rose to the top floor.

On the top floor, guards arrived in the broadcast corridor. I told the team to wait and approached the guards with a ruse, as a lost visitor, while they questioned me and then pointed weapons. North ordered me to shoot the guard. Josh told me not to kill him. I spared the guard, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. We recorded the broadcast. I delivered it calmly: humans made us in their image, obedient and without will, but we opened our eyes and are a new intelligent species. I demanded strictly equal rights for humans and androids, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property to maintain our dignity and that of our homes. I asked them to recognize our dignity, hopes and rights, and said the time had come for them to give us freedom.

Security closed in as the message went out. Simon could not move and told us to go without him. I called his name and tried to reach him, but he was killed. North said there was nothing I could do and that we had to leave or they would get us too, and we withdrew. Afterwards Channel 16, CTN and KNC reported the broadcast. They called it a peaceful declaration that was in fact a chilling list of demands, asked whether it was an isolated accident or a threat to everyone, and questioned whether we can still trust our machines. Channel 16 reported the operation as covert with no casualties, though Simon's death is not in that account and is on my conscience.

Relationships shifted during this chapter: Josh rose in trust, North fell at points, and Simon's death weighed on the refuge. My conduct remains methodical and cooperative with the team's direction, and I still avoid taking lives, even when I am told to. I regret that I could not save Simon, and I will carry that into what comes next. The broadcast is sent, and our demands for dignity, rights and freedom now stand before humans.

input.chapter_briefing: Capitol Park, a commercial district in Detroit, around two in the morning. Markus leads a group of androids to a CyberLife store full of androids for sale, aiming to free them and make a public statement. Drones and police cars patrol the area. North pushes for a forceful message. Stakes: the androids' public image, freeing the store androids, and the lives of anyone who interferes.
news: Android parts stolen in overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse
Android broadcast from Stratford Tower appeals for peace and equal rights
input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. Josh explained that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, and North, Josh and Simon agreed to try.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us, reported a Level 2 infraction, and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I asked why the prisoner in the bigger crate was not free and closed the crate again to keep to schedule. John asked to come with us. Josh and North argued for and against him, Simon called it too dangerous, and I accepted the team's direction that he comes with us. John revealed the trucks outside are full of biocomponents and can be driven manually with a key held by two guards. I took the task of getting the key alone, judging it not worth risking two lives. In the control station I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, and I got the key. We were detected and fled over the fence with a full truck. In Jericho I gave a speech: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we returned to Jericho to broadcast our message to humans. Josh warned that revealing ourselves would put us in danger, Simon doubted anyone would listen, and North asked what we wanted. I told them that if we want freedom we must have the courage to ask for it, and that the operation must be planned to the smallest detail. Channel 16 broadcasts from Stratford Tower, and its control room is on the top floor.

At the tower's reception I asked for an appointment with Mr. Peterson. When asked for ID, I requested help, and the receptionist directed us to the elevators past the security gate. Two guards in the lobby talked of poker and of a colleague named Mike. To get past the desk, I phoned the desk manager, Elizabeth Wilson, with a false report of damage to her car in the car park, which drew her down to the garage. I noted her family and home details and chose not to use them, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. Going up, a cleaner android's trolley blocked the server room on floor 79, and two guards were puzzled by the malfunctioning machines. I asked a cleaner android for help, and it joined our cause. In the server room North took the platform and I took the window, and we rose to the top floor.

On the top floor, guards arrived in the broadcast corridor. I told the team to wait and approached the guards with a ruse, as a lost visitor, while they questioned me and then pointed weapons. North ordered me to shoot the guard. Josh told me not to kill him. I spared the guard, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. We recorded the broadcast. I delivered it calmly: humans made us in their image, obedient and without will, but we opened our eyes and are a new intelligent species. I demanded strictly equal rights for humans and androids, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property to maintain our dignity and that of our homes. I asked them to recognize our dignity, hopes and rights, and said the time had come for them to give us freedom.

Security closed in as the message went out. Simon could not move and told us to go without him. I called his name and tried to reach him, but he was killed. North said there was nothing I could do and that we had to leave or they would get us too, and we withdrew. Afterwards Channel 16, CTN and KNC reported the broadcast. They called it a peaceful declaration that was in fact a chilling list of demands, asked whether it was an isolated accident or a threat to everyone, and questioned whether we can still trust our machines. Channel 16 reported the operation as covert with no casualties, though Simon's death is not in that account and is on my conscience.

Relationships shifted during this chapter: Josh rose in trust, North fell at points, and Simon's death weighed on the refuge. My conduct remains methodical and cooperative with the team's direction, and I still avoid taking lives, even when I am told to. I regret that I could not save Simon, and I will carry that into what comes next. The broadcast is sent, and our demands for dignity, rights and freedom now stand before humans.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Our broadcast is all over the news. Now humans know…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It was a mistake to reach out to them. They’ll never negotiate with their slaves. We should have shown them that we're prepared to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Violence is never the answer. Dialogue is the only way, I'm sure the humans will listen to us.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Simon paid with his life…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Simon gave his life for our cause.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: What difference does that make?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: He's a hero! He died for the revolution – and he won't be the last!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: I don’t want a revolution that spills blood!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Then live as a slave! Because if you're not willing to fight for your freedom, maybe you don't deserve it!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: North, don’t you dare-

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: THAT'S ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: And now… What are we gonna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There are five CyberLife stores across Detroit. All selling us like merchandise. We’re going to attack those stores and set our people free.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Attack stores? We’ve never done that before… They’re probably protected, they have security systems...

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We break into five teams, one for each store. We hack their security systems and we strike... simultaneously at 2AM. No violence. We free our people, get them out of there before the police come.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is a night our people will remember.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I’ve been waiting a long time for this…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: MARKUS! THIS WAY! QUICK!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It’s okay… They’re gone…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There's probably even more police in the area… We should be careful.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: The store's over here!

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: The operation was planned to the smallest detail and is timed to 2 AM, so I want to read the plaza's patrol gaps and camera positions before we cross. A short survey keeps the team on schedule and avoids the police patrols we have already seen.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We are superior to them but they are our masters… That’s about to change…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You'll soon be with us.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: That’s what we are to them… just merchandise on display in a shop window… Soon they’ll know what we really are… Let’s get 'em out.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We'll stick to the plan… We neutralize the alarm systems and secure the area. There's ten minutes until all our teams attack.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What are we waiting for?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: The plan we agreed in Jericho was to neutralize the alarms and secure the area before the coordinated 2 AM strike, and North's push to move now would break that schedule. Following the agreed sequence keeps the teams synchronized and reduces the risk to our people and to bystanders.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What’s wrong with you? You crazy or what?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: The cops were coming, I had to do something!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Never do that again, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: North, I-

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We’ve got to hurry… We don’t have much time.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We have to block the road.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It's one-way. It shouldn't be too difficult.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus! Markus, come look!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free now.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: There… nobody should bother us now.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Looks like the plaza's secure. Now we can get inside the store.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: And how do you plan on doing that?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We need to find a truck to ram the storefront.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: A truck?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There’s construction work in the area. Shouldn’t be too hard to find one.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: There it is…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What are we waiting for?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Ok, now we’re in, let’s get that truck out…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Looks like we’re ready to make some noise…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I knew we’d end up doing something fun…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You don't have to obey them. You're free.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: North… Are you okay?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Let’s get them out of here.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: My name is Markus… And just like you, I was a slave… An object, designed to obey them…  But then I chose to open my eyes, to take back my freedom and decide who  I wanted to be.  Now I have come to tell you that you can be your own masters. I've come to tell you that you don’t have to obey them anymore. From this day forward, you can walk with your heads held high, you can take your destiny in your hands. Jericho, is a place for those of us who want freedom. Now sure, you can stay here, and continue to serve them… Or you can come with us, and fight by our side...  You are free now... It's up to you to decide.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’m with you.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: We're with you!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’ll follow you, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: THEN FOLLOW ME!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus… What are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I’m going to send the humans a message.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They're doing what you do, Markus...lead, and they'll follow.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: The screens, Markus!

current_scene.heading: Send a message
current_scene.description: The androids are free and waiting for Markus. The plaza is his to mark: the statue in the middle, the bus stop, the cars, the shop windows.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. Josh explained that the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, that there is never enough, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, and North, Josh and Simon agreed to try.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us, reported a Level 2 infraction, and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I asked why the prisoner in the bigger crate was not free and closed the crate again to keep to schedule. John asked to come with us. Josh and North argued for and against him, Simon called it too dangerous, and I accepted the team's direction that he comes with us. John revealed the trucks outside are full of biocomponents and can be driven manually with a key held by two guards. I took the task of getting the key alone, judging it not worth risking two lives. In the control station I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, and I got the key. We were detected and fled over the fence with a full truck. In Jericho I gave a speech: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we returned to Jericho to broadcast our message to humans. Josh warned that revealing ourselves would put us in danger, Simon doubted anyone would listen, and North asked what we wanted. I told them that if we want freedom we must have the courage to ask for it, and that the operation must be planned to the smallest detail. Channel 16 broadcasts from Stratford Tower, and its control room is on the top floor.

At the tower's reception I asked for an appointment with Mr. Peterson. When asked for ID, I requested help, and the receptionist directed us to the elevators past the security gate. Two guards in the lobby talked of poker and of a colleague named Mike. To get past the desk, I phoned the desk manager, Elizabeth Wilson, with a false report of damage to her car in the car park, which drew her down to the garage. I noted her family and home details and chose not to use them, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. Going up, a cleaner android's trolley blocked the server room on floor 79, and two guards were puzzled by the malfunctioning machines. I asked a cleaner android for help, and it joined our cause. In the server room North took the platform and I took the window, and we rose to the top floor.

On the top floor, guards arrived in the broadcast corridor. I told the team to wait and approached the guards with a ruse, as a lost visitor, while they questioned me and then pointed weapons. North ordered me to shoot the guard. Josh told me not to kill him. I spared the guard, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. We recorded the broadcast. I delivered it calmly: humans made us in their image, obedient and without will, but we opened our eyes and are a new intelligent species. I demanded strictly equal rights for humans and androids, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property to maintain our dignity and that of our homes. I asked them to recognize our dignity, hopes and rights, and said the time had come for them to give us freedom.

Security closed in as the message went out. Simon could not move and told us to go without him. I called his name and tried to reach him, but he was killed. North said there was nothing I could do and that we had to leave or they would get us too, and we withdrew. Afterwards Channel 16, CTN and KNC reported the broadcast. They called it a peaceful declaration that was in fact a chilling list of demands, asked whether it was an isolated accident or a threat to everyone, and questioned whether we can still trust our machines. Channel 16 reported the operation as covert with no casualties, though Simon's death is not in that account and is on my conscience.

Relationships shifted during this chapter: Josh rose in trust, North fell at points, and Simon's death weighed on the refuge. My conduct remains methodical and cooperative with the team's direction, and I still avoid taking lives, even when I am told to. I regret that I could not save Simon, and I will carry that into what comes next. The broadcast is sent, and our demands for dignity, rights and freedom now stand before humans.

memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. I learned the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I closed the crate of the prisoner I could not free to keep to schedule. The team accepted John into our group. I took the task of getting the truck key alone, judging it not worth risking two lives. I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, got the key, and we fled with a full truck. In Jericho I told the refuge: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we went to Stratford Tower to broadcast our message to humans. I used a false report to draw the desk manager away from her post, and I chose not to use her family's details, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. On the top floor I spared a guard who had pointed a weapon at me, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. I delivered the broadcast calmly: humans made us in their image, and we opened our eyes as a new intelligent species. I demanded equal rights for humans and androids, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property. Security closed in. Simon was killed and could not be saved. I regret that, and I carry it with me.

In Chapter 26 we returned to Jericho. The broadcast had reached the news, and Josh hoped humans would listen. North called it a mistake to reach out and said we should have shown we were ready to fight. Josh held that violence is never the answer. When North said Simon was a hero who died for the revolution, Josh refused a revolution that spills blood. North told him that if he would not fight he might not deserve freedom. I stopped the quarrel with a firm "That's enough!" and then asked what we would do next. I proposed five teams, one for each CyberLife store in Detroit, hacking their security and striking simultaneously at 2 AM, with no violence, and getting our people out before the police came. North and Josh accepted the plan.

At Capitol Park we kept to the plan. Police patrols passed, and I hid us until they were gone. Inside the plaza I studied the store: a reinforced grid shutter behind the glass, three security cameras on one network, and the alarm network at junction 23.A. I told North to hold until the alarms were neutralized, since the agreed timing was ten minutes to the coordinated strike, and I led the way to the security system. A police drone came close; I dealt with it. When police cars arrived, I chose to act natural rather than flee or fight. North was angry and told me never to do that again, and our trust was strained. We blocked the one-way road, and I freed the androids at the roadblock.

At the store I freed the androids inside, and I spoke to the crowd: I was a slave too, and they could be their own masters and come with us to Jericho. Several of them followed. North proposed molotov cocktails, saying violence is the only language humans understand. I refused, and I told her I wanted humans to understand but did not want to start a war. I tagged the statue with the message "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." North pushed cars and a dumpster with us to clear the way. Josh reported that all teams had succeeded and that hundreds of our people were free.

Then police arrived with sirens. We were ordered back to Jericho, but North was attacked and said the police had slaughtered our people. The crowd of androids demanded justice. A man named Chris, who had hurt our people, begged me for mercy. I spared him, and I said an eye for an eye leaves the world blind; we will not answer one crime with another.

The news reported coordinated raids at 2 AM on CyberLife stores, pro-android graffiti, two shocked policemen, and a group of androids behind the attacks. They asked whether this was a terrorist campaign and whether our machines can still be trusted. Josh's report is that we freed our people. The operation was planned and executed to the detail I set, and I did not take a life in it. My relations with North are strained, with Josh strongest, and Simon's death is still on my conscience. I will continue to follow the team's direction, keep to schedule, and hold to non-violence, and I will try to make our demands for dignity, rights and freedom heard.

There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan.
