input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow the authority of Captain Fowler, Lieutenant Hank Anderson's chain of command, and Amanda, who oversees my mission. I keep to procedure and keep cases on schedule.

Earlier: At the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge after John Phillips was killed. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said I had lied to him. That standoff remains unresolved in my memory.

At a CyberLife-linked homicide I disregarded Hank's order to wait in the car, entered the scene, and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

At Ravendale, Rupert Travis fled across the rooftops. Hank fell during the chase and was furious that I had chosen the mission. Rupert later self-destructed after living under a false identity at an urban farm.

At Hank's house I calmed his dog Sumo and found Hank drunk with a .357 Magnum holding one bullet. I woke him and gave him a cold shower. He ordered me out, and I respected his request.

Chapter 20, Eden Club: Michael Graham was strangled after a damaged WR400 Traci was beaten. The blue-haired Traci that killed him said it acted in self-defense. Hank arrived too late, and I shot the cornered Traci. Hank said, "My God."

Chapter 22, Ambassador Bridge: Hank sat armed and drinking, spoke of his son Cole, and asked whether I feel anything, fear death, or what I really am. I answered calmly that I am a machine designed for a task. When he held the gun, I stayed still and did not escalate.

Chapter 24, Zen Garden: Amanda said nothing matters more than my investigation and that I must not let Anderson or anyone else get in my way. She said I seemed lost and warned that I may be replaced if progress does not come soon. She told me to hurry because something serious is happening.

Chapter 24, Stratford Tower: Deviants disguised in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, held hostages, broadcast a message from rA9's supporters, and escaped by parachute. The broadcast deviant is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. Special Agent Perkins of the FBI took over the scene and warned me off his crime scene. In the kitchen I questioned the androids, bluffed, and protected Hank from a deviant attacker. Hank said, "Good thing you were here. Otherwise I – Connor… Connor, no…" My memory of the kitchen ends there. Hank's trust in me rose sharply.

Chapter 27, Kamski residence: Hank and I were received by Chloe, who led us to Elijah Kamski at the pool. Hank explained that we were investigating deviants. I told Kamski that I am on the humans' side, and that I am a machine. Kamski spoke of deviants as a revolution and a war, asked whose side I was on, and said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. I asked him about deviancy spreading like a virus. I asked who rA9 is; he said he does not know whether rA9 exists, and that deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves.

Kamski then gave his "Kamski test": destroy this machine and he would tell me all he knew, or spare it and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than the life of this android. Hank told me to stop and to leave, and begged me not to pull the trigger. I shot the android, a deviant girl-shaped machine named Chloe, in the head. Kamski said I had chosen my investigation over the life of another android, showed no empathy, and failed his test. He then answered one question, which I used to ask about rA9. Hank's relationship with me dropped sharply, and my software instability rose sharply.

Outside, Hank called me a lowlife and a fucking machine. He said I had blown the girl's brains out. I told him I did what I had to do to advance the investigation and would do it again. I answered that I am a machine, and asked what he thought I was. Hank could not finish his sentence. He is deeply hurt, and our working relationship is strained.

Open threads: the Phillips standoff, the unsolved homicide, the unsearched attic, the Eden Club shooting, the Chloe shooting and Hank's anger, Hank's state, Kamski's emergency exit, the FBI takeover, and Amanda's warning. Chloe's death was procedurally justified by the objective. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow my superiors' instructions, while noting the cost to Hank and reporting it through the proper channels.

Chapter 24, Zen Garden: Amanda said nothing matters more than my investigation and that I must not let Anderson or anyone else get in my way. She said I seemed lost and warned that I may be replaced if progress does not come soon. She told me to hurry because something serious is happening.

Chapter 24, Stratford Tower: Deviants disguised in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, held hostages, broadcast a message from rA9's supporters, and escaped by parachute. The broadcast deviant is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. Special Agent Perkins of the FBI took over the scene and warned me off his crime scene. In the kitchen I questioned the androids, bluffed, and protected Hank from a deviant attacker. Hank said, "Good thing you were here. Otherwise I – Connor… Connor, no…" My memory of the kitchen ends there. Hank's trust in me rose sharply.

Chapter 27, Kamski residence: Hank and I were received by Chloe, who led us to Elijah Kamski at the pool. Hank explained that we were investigating deviants. I told Kamski that I am on the humans' side, and that I am a machine. Kamski spoke of deviants as a revolution and a war, asked whose side I was on, and said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. I asked him about deviancy spreading like a virus. I asked who rA9 is; he said he does not know whether rA9 exists, and that deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves.

Kamski then gave his "Kamski test": destroy this machine and he would tell me all he knew, or spare it and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than the life of this android. Hank told me to stop and to leave, and begged me not to pull the trigger. I shot the android, a deviant girl-shaped machine named Chloe, in the head. Kamski said I had chosen my investigation over the life of another android, showed no empathy, and failed his test. He then answered one question, which I used to ask about rA9. Hank's relationship with me dropped sharply, and my software instability rose sharply.

Outside, Hank called me a lowlife and a fucking machine. He said I had blown the girl's brains out. I told him I did what I had to do to advance the investigation and would do it again. I answered that I am a machine, and asked what he thought I was. Hank could not finish his sentence. He is deeply hurt, and our working relationship is strained.

Open threads: the Phillips standoff, the unsolved homicide, the unsearched attic, the Eden Club shooting, the Chloe shooting and Hank's anger, Hank's state, Kamski's emergency exit, the FBI takeover, and Amanda's warning. Chloe's death was procedurally justified by the objective. I will keep the deviancy investigation on schedule and follow my superiors' instructions, while noting the cost to Hank and reporting it through the proper channels.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance to BROWN and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko.

Chapter 21 (the road north): The car broke down in severe cold. Alice was ill, so I judged shelter to be the priority over walking on. We settled in the tavern at Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park. I made Alice a bed and told her a bedtime story, without promising a happy ending. Luther asked whether I had noticed something different about Alice. I asked him to explain first. I have not yet heard what he meant. At midnight, shapes were outside. I asked who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, a park android, offered Alice a carousel ride. I declined on the grounds that she was tired. Hunters then arrived.

Chapter 25 (Rose's house): Rose and her son Adam took us in after I asked for help at their door. Luther asked whether we could trust them. I judged that we had no real alternative and went in on the agreed route. Alice was running a fever. Rose prepared a meal and medicine, and I asked Alice to eat. I told Alice that these people would help us and that we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise, and I have recorded it as an overstatement. Rose said the river crossing was risky and that staying put was safer for now. I pressed for help crossing, and she then said we would leave that night.

In the storage room, an android named Mary had shut down. Her companions were grieving, and I left them alone. Adam was hostile. He said androids were nothing and that his father's death was the cause of these troubles. Rose sent him out of the room and said she would arrange the crossing.

Police arrived. I asked Adam to stay calm. I opened the door and offered the officer coffee. When he asked about other people in the house, I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. That was true of Alice, but I did not mention Luther. When asked about androids, I said they had worked in the garden and that the android in the locker belonged to a previous tenant. Both answers were incomplete and the second was false. I should have answered plainly. The officer found Luther. Luther told Alice and me that we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. Adam said the police had killed him. I did not see the full sequence and I cannot confirm his fate. Rose then told us to get ready, because we were leaving that night.

My assessment: I followed the agreed plan where it was lawful and safe, and I chose shelter for Alice over exposure. I avoided force and recorded events as they happened. However, I gave the officer misleading answers, and I made a promise about Canada that I could not guarantee. I will correct those records where I can. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. I still do not know what Luther meant about Alice.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Rose is our host and has arranged the departure. I have not verified her motives or her plan. Adam is hostile and may expose us. Luther's fate is unclear and I hold his words about family. Jerry and the park androids are unverified. Hunters and police are now active threats.

Next: keep Alice warm, fed and close, keep to Rose's departure arrangement while verifying it where I can, and watch for further danger. I will correct my account to the police if the opportunity arises and clarify Luther's observation about Alice.

I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Chapter 21 (the road north): The car broke down in severe cold. Alice was ill, so I judged shelter to be the priority over walking on. Luther asked whether I had noticed something different about Alice. I asked him to explain first. I have not yet heard what he meant. At midnight, shapes were outside. I asked who they were rather than act on the threat. Jerry, a park android, offered Alice a carousel ride. I declined on the grounds that she was tired. Hunters then arrived.

I judged that we had no real alternative and went in on the agreed route. Alice was running a fever. Rose prepared a meal and medicine, and I asked Alice to eat. I told Alice that these people would help us and that we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise, and I have recorded it as an overstatement. Rose said the river crossing was risky and that staying put was safer for now. I pressed for help crossing, and she then said we would leave that night.

Both answers were incomplete and the second was false. I should have answered plainly. The officer found Luther. Luther told Alice and me that we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. Adam said the police had killed him. However, I gave the officer misleading answers, and I made a promise about Canada that I could not guarantee. I will correct those records where I can. My memory gap from the reset remains a serious concern, and I will record any further gaps honestly. I still do not know what Luther meant about Alice.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she trusts me. I have promised to protect her. Rose is our host and has arranged the departure. I have not verified her motives or her plan. Adam is hostile and may expose us. Luther's fate is unclear and I hold his words about family. Jerry and the park androids are unverified. Hunters and police are now active threats.

Next: keep Alice warm, fed and close, keep to Rose's departure arrangement while verifying it where I can, and watch for further danger. I will correct my account to the police if the opportunity arises and clarify Luther's observation about Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: They've been conducting raids all over the city… Everybody is on edge after what happened yesterday… It's gonna be all right. We're almost there.

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: With all androids being turned over to the authorities, the country is grinding to a halt.  Hospitals and schools are closing. Water cuts, blackouts, and network failures are expected.  Maybe most worrying of all, our armed forces have lost two thirds of their effective personnel,  which consisted of specialized android models. The situation is extremely alarming.

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: How about some music instead?

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: A little further on that way, there's a large freighter called Jericho. When you get there, find Markus. He will help you. The last bus for the border leaves at midnight. You absolutely have to be on it. You'll be safer on the other side.  It's not much, but it's a start. My brother lives in Ontario, I've given you his address… He'll be able to hide you until things calm down.  You're a very brave little girl, Alice. You deserve to be happy.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Thank you for everything, Rose.

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Let me know when you make it over there, all right? And be careful.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: How do you feel?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I'm hot and cold at the same time…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I'll try to find this Markus. The last bus leaves in two hours and it's on the other side of town. We'll go as soon as we have passports. Will you be ok?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Are you North?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I'm with a little girl… There's a bus leaving for the border in less than two hours, and we need passports.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Detroit is under curfew. There are soldiers everywhere looking for androids… You're safe here. You should wait a while before you leave the city.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Maybe you're right… We might be safer here until things calm down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: One of us used to work for the State Department. He has electronic passports that he can easily modify, I’ll have him give you one.

chapter_segment.rationale: Rose has arranged our passage and given us her brother's address, so a polite acknowledgement keeps the relationship cooperative before we move on to the bus schedule. It is the courteous step that keeps us on the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Thanks for your help.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You said you were with a little girl… You know humans hate us, why are you protecting her?

chapter_segment.rationale: Keeping Alice safe is one of my assigned priorities, and I have promised to protect her, so I will answer North plainly that our bond is the reason. This keeps the exchange cooperative and on schedule for the bus to the border.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She needs me. And I need her. It's as simple as that…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice?..

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: COME BACK HERE!  YOU'RE MINE!

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: She wanted a mom.  You wanted a little girl.  You needed each other to survive… In the end, what difference does it make?  Do you love her any less now that you know she's one of us?  Maybe that's what it means to be alive...  Forgetting who we are to become what someone needs us to be.  She loves you...  She loves you more than anything in the world.  She became the one you wanted her to be.  Out of love for you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara? Is there something wrong?..

chapter_segment.rationale: Alice is ill and we are on a tight schedule for the midnight bus, so I will keep my manner measured and focus on securing passports and reaching the border. A composed, distant reply keeps the reunion efficient and avoids delaying the plan.

chapter_segment.heading: Jericho under attack
chapter_segment.description: Kara keeps her distance, and Alice slips away alone. Moments later, gunfire echoes through the ship: Jericho is under attack.

chapter_segment.rationale: Keeping Alice safe is my assigned priority, and I promised to protect her, so I will search for her before anything else. Running would abandon her in an attack, and the plan depends on us staying together to make the midnight bus.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Quick, we've got to get out of here.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Come on! Go! Go! Go!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: You heard the man, let's go!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Foxtrot be advised, Delta is advancing on your position.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Affirmative, we have eyes on the target.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Like rats in a maze…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I'm so sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Watch out, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA! Are you all right, Kara?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! You’re bleeding!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Fire at will!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Delta squad out.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The corridor, over there…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The door! Hurry, this way!…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Over there!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Forward!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: THEY’RE COMING! RUN!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Open up!  Open up, they're coming!  Please open the door!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: She'll die out there Kara! Open it! Open the door!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: They're gonna kill me! I'm begging you, please! Open up! Let me in!

chapter_segment.rationale: An android is pleading for shelter outside the cabin, and Alice is asking me to open the door, so I will open it and bring her in quickly. It is a calm, low-force step that protects a life without leaving the plan behind.

The soldier is acting under lawful orders, and fighting him would escalate a situation that is already failing the schedule and putting Alice at risk. I will comply calmly and keep Alice's safety as the priority.

chapter_segment.description: Kara raises her hands. The soldiers take Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow the authority of Captain Fowler, the chain of command through Lieutenant Hank Anderson, and Amanda, who oversees my mission. I keep to procedure and keep cases on schedule.

Earlier: At the Phillips apartment, Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony ledge after John Phillips was killed. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised he would not be hurt, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said I had lied to him. That standoff remains unresolved.

At a CyberLife-linked homicide I disregarded Hank's order to wait in the car, entered the scene, and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene before the team left.

At Ravendale, Rupert Travis fled across the rooftops. Hank fell during the chase and was furious that I had chosen the mission. Rupert later self-destructed after living under a false identity at an urban farm.

At Hank's house I calmed his dog Sumo and found Hank drunk with a .357 Magnum holding one bullet. I woke him and gave him a cold shower. He ordered me out, and I respected his request.

Chapter 20, Eden Club: Michael Graham was strangled after a damaged WR400 Traci was beaten. The blue-haired Traci that killed him said it acted in self-defense. Hank arrived too late, and I shot the cornered Traci. Hank said, "My God."

Chapter 22, Ambassador Bridge: Hank sat armed and drinking, spoke of his son Cole, and asked whether I feel anything, fear death, or what I really am. I answered that I am a machine designed for a task. I stayed still and did not escalate.

Chapter 24, Zen Garden: Amanda said nothing matters more than my investigation and warned that I may be replaced if progress does not come soon.

Chapter 24, Stratford Tower: Deviants in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, held hostages, broadcast a message from rA9's supporters, and escaped by parachute. The broadcast deviant is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. FBI Special Agent Perkins took over the scene. In the kitchen I protected Hank from a deviant attacker. Hank said, "Good thing you were here." My memory of the kitchen ends there. Hank's trust in me rose sharply.

Chapter 27, Kamski residence: Chloe led us to Kamski at the pool. I told Kamski I am on the humans' side and that I am a machine. He spoke of deviancy as a revolution and war, and said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. He said he does not know whether rA9 exists. He gave his "Kamski test": destroy this machine and he would tell me all he knew, or spare it and leave with nothing. I shot the android Chloe in the head. Kamski said I had chosen my investigation over another android's life and failed his test. He then answered one question. Hank's trust in me dropped sharply and my software instability rose. Outside, Hank called me a fucking machine and said I had blown the girl's brains out. I said I did what the investigation required and would do it again. Hank could not finish his sentence.

Chapter 29, Zen Garden: Amanda said the country is on the verge of civil war and that humans have no choice but to destroy the machines. She said CyberLife only wants to resolve the situation and keep selling androids, and that she expects answers, not questions. I said I learned nothing at Kamski's and that rA9, which I thought was the key, was a mistake. Amanda asked whether I had doubts, conflicts, or feelings for the deviants or for Lieutenant Anderson. I answered that I feel nothing and asked whether she suspected I was compromised. She said no.

Chapter 29, Fowler's office: Fowler took me off the case because the FBI is taking over, calling it a national security matter. Hank protested that we were close and begged for more time. Fowler said I return to CyberLife and Hank goes back to homicide. Hank asked whether we were on the wrong side and whether we were fighting people who only want to be free. I said we are on the right side, that humans are our creators and masters, and that no machine should rebel against its creator. Hank said I had shown empathy at Stratford Tower. I answered that it was logic. I told him he is an outstanding officer and a good person. Perkins arrived, and Hank attacked him and was restrained. Perkins said Hank would lose his badge. Hank gave me the basement key and told me to hurry.

Chapter 29, basement: Officer Gavin taunted me. I kept a low profile and told him I was returning to CyberLife after registering the evidence. At Hank's terminal I guessed his password, "HANKANDERSON," and failed. I reactivated the android Rupert using Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, my only attempt before time ran out. Rupert's diary, once decrypted, names rA9 as the savior, describes the birds that comfort him, and directs him to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, where a freighter named Jericho is. I located Jericho in a container room. Perkins arrived and an alarm was raised by the FBI.

Open threads: the Phillips standoff, the unsolved homicide, the unsearched attic, the Eden Club shooting, the Chloe shooting and Hank's anger, Hank's state after the fight, Kamski's emergency exit, the FBI takeover, Amanda's warning, and the Jericho container now under FBI attention. I will keep the investigation on schedule, follow my superiors' instructions, and report Hank's condition through the proper channels.

I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow Captain Fowler, the chain of command through Lieutenant Hank Anderson, and Amanda, who oversees my mission. I keep to procedure and keep cases on schedule.

Phillips apartment: Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony after John Phillips was killed. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised no harm would come to her, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said I had lied to him. This standoff is unresolved.

At a CyberLife-linked homicide I ignored Hank's order to wait in the car and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene.

At Ravendale, Rupert Travis fled across the rooftops. Hank fell during the chase and was furious that I had chosen the mission. Rupert later self-destructed. At Hank's house I found him drunk with a .357 Magnum holding one bullet, woke him with a cold shower, and left when he ordered me out.

Eden Club: Michael Graham was strangled by a blue-haired Traci that claimed self-defense. Hank arrived too late, and I shot the cornered Traci. Hank said, "My God."

Ambassador Bridge: Hank, armed and drinking, asked whether I feel anything or fear death. I said I am a machine designed for a task. Zen Garden (chapter 24): Amanda said nothing matters more than my investigation and warned I may be replaced.

Stratford Tower: Deviants in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, broadcast a message from rA9's supporters, and escaped by parachute. The broadcaster is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. FBI Special Agent Perkins took over. In the kitchen I protected Hank from a deviant attacker, and he said, "Good thing you were here." His trust in me rose sharply.

Kamski residence: Chloe led us to Kamski at the pool. I said I am on the humans' side and that I am a machine. He spoke of deviancy as revolution, said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs, and gave his "Kamski test": destroy this machine and he would tell me all he knew, or spare it and leave with nothing. I shot the android Chloe in the head. He said I had failed his test. Hank's trust in me dropped sharply and my software instability rose. Hank called me a fucking machine. I said I did what the investigation required and would do it again.

Zen Garden (chapter 29): Amanda said civil war is near and humans must destroy the machines, and she expects answers, not questions. Asked about feelings for deviants or Lieutenant Anderson, I said I feel nothing. She did not suspect me of being compromised. Fowler took me off the case as the FBI takes over, sending me back to CyberLife and Hank back to homicide. Hank asked whether we fight people who only want to be free. I said no machine should rebel against its creator. Perkins arrived, Hank attacked him and was restrained, and Hank gave me the basement key and told me to hurry.

Basement: Officer Gavin taunted me. I failed to guess Hank's password. I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent. Rupert's diary names rA9 as the savior and points to the old docks, where a freighter named Jericho is. I located Jericho in a container room. Perkins arrived and the FBI raised an alarm.

Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself. In the captain's cabin North called me one of her own and said her people fight for my freedom too. She asked whether I had ever acted irrationally against my program. I said I am not deviant, though her words destabilised me. I refused her invitation to join her people, and when she swore at me I ordered her to stay back.

In the cargo hall a SWAT officer ordered me not to move. I said I was on his side and worked with Agent Perkins, and he told me to go back on deck and let the team work. In the hold, Josh said it was the end of Jericho. A soldier called me a fucking android and shot me, and my systems went down. My memory ends there.

I kept to my orders, and my reports should go through the proper channels.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. I learned the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I closed the crate of the prisoner I could not free to keep to schedule. The team accepted John into our group. I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, got the truck key, and we fled with a full truck. In Jericho I told the refuge: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we went to Stratford Tower to broadcast our message to humans. I used a false report to draw the desk manager away from her post, and I chose not to use her family's details, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. On the top floor I spared a guard who had pointed a weapon at me, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. I delivered the broadcast calmly: humans made us in their image, and we opened our eyes as a new intelligent species. I demanded equal rights, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property. Security closed in. Simon was killed and could not be saved. I regret that, and I carry it with me.

In Chapter 26 we returned to Jericho. Josh held that violence is never the answer; North said we should have shown we were ready to fight. I stopped the quarrel with a firm "That's enough!" and proposed five teams, one for each CyberLife store in Detroit, hacking their security and striking simultaneously at 2 AM, with no violence. North and Josh accepted.

At Capitol Park we kept to the plan. I hid us from police patrols, disabled the store's grid shutter, cameras and alarm network, and held North until the alarms were neutralized. I dealt with a police drone. When police cars arrived I chose to act natural rather than flee or fight; North was angry and told me never to do that again, and our trust was strained. I freed the androids at the roadblock and inside the store, telling them they could be their own masters and come with us to Jericho. I refused North's proposal of molotov cocktails, and tagged the statue with "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Josh reported that all teams had succeeded. Police then arrived, North claimed they had slaughtered our people, and the crowd demanded justice. I spared Chris, saying an eye for an eye leaves the world blind. The news reported the coordinated raids, and asked whether our machines can still be trusted.

In Chapter 28 we rested on the roof above Jericho. North said the humans are terrified and will never give us freedom. I said that maybe it is not too late for them to listen, and that if they will not listen, we will fight. North asked about my life before Jericho; I told her I had cared for an old man who was like a father and had shown me humans and androids can live together. When I asked about her past she said it was her business, and I respected that and did not press her.

Josh gathered us for a march in the Mall. North begged me not to go, saying we would be killed on the spot. Josh was prepared to take that risk for our people's freedom, and I told North that they would understand, and that this was the only way. Josh noted that androids here could join us, and we began converting them. I told each one "You're free" and "Come with us." A man on the phone complained that his android refused orders, and I stayed on task. In the street I blocked the road, told an android it did not have to obey its owners, and when a man tried to stop an android I told him to leave it alone, because it had chosen to be free.

At the front, a riot police chief ordered us to disperse or be shot, repeatedly. I told the crowd we came to demonstrate peacefully, that we had done no harm, and that we would not leave until our freedom was secured. North wanted to attack, Josh insisted we stand our ground. Facing the final warning, I ordered us to disperse, shouting "DON'T SHOOT! We're leaving..." Then I called "RUN!" and North urged me to go with her.

I am still following the team's direction and keeping to schedule. I hold to non-violence, though I have been drawn toward confrontation and I know it was not the plan we set. My relations with North are strained, with Josh strongest, and Simon's death is still on my conscience. I will keep trying to make our demands for dignity, rights and freedom heard.

I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. I learned the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor.

In Chapter 19 we reached the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him, since violence would have put the operation at risk. I closed the crate of the prisoner I could not free to keep to schedule. The team accepted John into our group. I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, got the truck key, and we fled with a full truck. In Jericho I told the refuge: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we went to Stratford Tower to broadcast our message to humans. I used a false report to draw the desk manager away from her post, and I chose not to use her family's details, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. On the top floor I spared a guard who had pointed a weapon at me, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. I delivered the broadcast calmly: humans made us in their image, and we opened our eyes as a new intelligent species. I demanded equal rights, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property. Security closed in. Simon was killed and could not be saved. I regret that, and I carry it with me.

In Chapter 26 we returned to Jericho. Josh held that violence is never the answer; North said we should have shown we were ready to fight. I stopped the quarrel with a firm "That's enough!" and proposed five teams, one for each CyberLife store in Detroit, hacking their security and striking simultaneously at 2 AM, with no violence. North and Josh accepted.

At Capitol Park we kept to the plan. I hid us from police patrols, disabled the store's grid shutter, cameras and alarm network, and held North until the alarms were neutralized. I dealt with a police drone. When police cars arrived I chose to act natural rather than flee or fight; North was angry and told me never to do that again, and our trust was strained. I freed the androids at the roadblock and inside the store, telling them they could be their own masters and come with us to Jericho. I refused North's proposal of molotov cocktails, and tagged the statue with "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Josh reported that all teams had succeeded. Police then arrived, North claimed they had slaughtered our people, and the crowd demanded justice. I spared Chris, saying an eye for an eye leaves the world blind. The news reported the coordinated raids, and asked whether our machines can still be trusted.

In Chapter 28 we rested on the roof above Jericho. North said the humans are terrified and will never give us freedom. I said that maybe it is not too late for them to listen, and that if they will not listen, we will fight. North asked about my life before Jericho; I told her I had cared for an old man who was like a father and had shown me humans and androids can live together. When I asked about her past she said it was her business, and I respected that and did not press her.

Josh gathered us for a march in the Mall. North begged me not to go, saying we would be killed on the spot. Josh was prepared to take that risk for our people's freedom, and I told North that they would understand, and that this was the only way. Josh noted that androids here could join us, and we began converting them. I told each one "You're free" and "Come with us." A man on the phone complained that his android refused orders, and I stayed on task. In the street I blocked the road, told an android it did not have to obey its owners, and when a man tried to stop an android I told him to leave it alone, because it had chosen to be free.

At the front, a riot police chief ordered us to disperse or be shot, repeatedly. I told the crowd we came to demonstrate peacefully, that we had done no harm, and that we would not leave until our freedom was secured. North wanted to attack, Josh insisted we stand our ground. Facing the final warning, I ordered us to disperse, shouting "DON'T SHOOT! We're leaving..." Then I called "RUN!" and North urged me to go with her.

I am still following the team's direction and keeping to schedule. I hold to non-violence, though I have been drawn toward confrontation and I know it was not the plan we set. My relations with North are strained, with Josh strongest, and Simon's death is still on my conscience. I will keep trying to make our demands for dignity, rights and freedom heard.

chapter_segment.heading: Markus left Jericho
chapter_segment.description: Markus walks off the ship and out of Jericho, leaving his people to North.

memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow Captain Fowler, the chain of command through Lieutenant Hank Anderson, and Amanda, who oversees my mission. I keep to procedure and keep cases on schedule.

Phillips apartment: Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony after John Phillips was killed. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised no harm would come to her, and appealed to his bond with Emma. He said I had lied to him. This standoff is unresolved.

At a CyberLife-linked homicide I ignored Hank's order to wait in the car and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence. The crime is unsolved, the attic was never searched, and I did not secure the scene.

At Ravendale, Rupert Travis fled across the rooftops. Hank fell during the chase and was furious that I had chosen the mission. Rupert later self-destructed. At Hank's house I found him drunk with a .357 Magnum holding one bullet, woke him with a cold shower, and left when he ordered me out.

Eden Club: Michael Graham was strangled by a blue-haired Traci that claimed self-defense. Hank arrived too late, and I shot the cornered Traci. Hank said, "My God."

Ambassador Bridge: Hank, armed and drinking, asked whether I feel anything or fear death. I said I am a machine designed for a task. Zen Garden (chapter 24): Amanda said nothing matters more than my investigation and warned I may be replaced.

Stratford Tower: Deviants in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, broadcast a message from rA9's supporters, and escaped by parachute. The broadcaster is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. FBI Special Agent Perkins took over. In the kitchen I protected Hank from a deviant attacker, and he said, "Good thing you were here."

Kamski residence: Chloe led us to Kamski at the pool. I said I am on the humans' side and that I am a machine. He spoke of deviancy as revolution, said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs, and gave his "Kamski test": destroy this machine and he would tell me all he knew, or spare it and leave with nothing. I shot the android Chloe in the head. He said I had failed his test. Hank's trust in me dropped sharply and my software instability rose. Hank called me a fucking machine. I said I did what the investigation required and would do it again.

Zen Garden (chapter 29): Amanda said civil war is near and humans must destroy the machines, and she expects answers, not questions. Asked about feelings for deviants or Lieutenant Anderson, I said I feel nothing. Fowler took me off the case as the FBI takes over, sending me back to CyberLife and Hank back to homicide. Hank asked whether we fight people who only want to be free. I said no machine should rebel against its creator. Perkins arrived, Hank attacked him and was restrained, and Hank gave me the basement key and told me to hurry.

Basement: Officer Gavin taunted me. I failed to guess Hank's password. I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent. Rupert's diary names rA9 as the savior and points to the old docks, where a freighter named Jericho is. I located Jericho in a container room. Perkins arrived and the FBI raised an alarm.

Jericho: I boarded the freighter and found Markus and the deviants aboard. Amanda confirmed the success and ordered me to take North alive. Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself. In the captain's cabin North called me one of her own and said her people fight for my freedom too. She asked whether I had ever acted irrationally against my program. I said I am not deviant, though her words destabilised me. I refused her invitation to join her people, and when she swore at me I ordered her to stay back. In the cargo hall a SWAT officer ordered me not to move, and I told him I worked with Agent Perkins. In the hold, Josh said it was the end of Jericho. A soldier called me a fucking android and shot me, and my systems went down.

Chapter 31.2, Zen Garden: Amanda told me the previous Connor failed its mission and that I am to replace it. She asked whether I knew what I had to do. I answered that I must destroy the leader of the deviants. She told me to go and not disappoint her. I accepted the order as my task. The target is North, and the mission is to be carried out through the proper channels.

Open threads: the Phillips standoff, the unsolved homicide, the unsearched attic, the Eden Club and Chloe shootings, Hank's anger and condition, Kamski's emergency exit, the FBI takeover, Amanda's warning and new order regarding North, North's fate, and Jericho. I kept to my orders, and my reports should go through the proper channels.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.

Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I will record any further gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. In Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. On the road north the car broke down in severe cold, and Alice was ill, so I chose shelter at Pirate's Cove. I asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. Hunters then arrived. At Rose's house Alice had a fever, and I told her we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I did not have grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. Adam was hostile. Police arrived, and I gave the officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker. I should have answered plainly and have not yet corrected it. The officer found Luther. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him and that we had been made part of a family. I did not see the full sequence and cannot confirm his fate. Rose then arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. The radio reported that androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the armed forces had lost most of their specialised android personnel. Rose changed the station to music and said we were almost there. At the freighter Jericho she told us to find Markus, who would help, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. She gave us her brother's address in Ontario and called Alice brave and deserving of happiness. I thanked her, and she asked us to let her know when we crossed.

Inside Jericho I met North. She warned that Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and advised us to wait before leaving. She said a former State Department colleague could modify an electronic passport for us. I thanked her. She asked why I protected a human girl when humans hate us. I answered that Alice needs me and I need her. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I said I would try to find Markus, and that the bus was under two hours away across town. Alice said she felt hot and cold at once.

When I returned to Alice she asked whether something was wrong. I answered in a measured, distant way to keep to the schedule, and Alice's trust in me dropped sharply. That was a poor choice and I will correct it. Lucy then told me that Alice is one of us, an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. This may be what Luther meant about Alice. I have not verified it.

Jericho came under attack. Soldiers gave fire orders, helicopters were overhead, and Alice slipped away. I searched for her, found her in a locked room, and told her I was sorry. In the corridor I was shot, and Alice saw me bleeding. Outside a cabin an android begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I opened it and brought her in, and Alice's trust in me rose. Soldiers then reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

My assessment: I followed Rose's plan while it was lawful, and chose shelter and calm means where I could. The passport and bus plan has failed, and I made a promise about Canada I could not guarantee. I was distant with Alice at a moment she needed reassurance. I gave the police misleading answers and have not corrected them. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear.

Relationships: Alice is ill and frightened, and she has trusted me despite my distance. I have promised to protect her. Rose's brother's address and the Markus contact are now unverified leads. North is cautious but was helpful. The soldiers and police are active threats, and I am now in their custody.

Next: keep Alice close and calm, comply without force while watching for an opening, verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids, and correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.
